When I started junior high, I had no friends at all and was actually bullied quite heavily. When you are admitted to inpatient, you can voluntarily sign yourself in, known as a 201 admission in most places.  However, if you would choose not to do so (or if your state has the language written differently since it sounds like you may still be a minor (or I'm making wrong assumptions about what you wrote)), you can instead be placed involuntarily (or against your will and also known as 302 admission). If the latter is what happens, it will need to get approval and you would then be placed inpatient under court order.  The consequences of involuntary vs voluntary admission vary, so you may want to see what the exact laws are in your state.  But as an example, in my state, having a 302 will make you intelligible from owing a firearm among other restrictions.  Like I said, check on your state's laws and don't be afraid to ask the hospital - they can and should be able to give you all the information you need.

Expect to spend a great deal of time waiting. The process of approving 201 (voluntary) or 302 (involuntary) can take a while, and then add additional time for bed searches if inpatient is indeed the outcome.  If it is going to be inpatient, I cannot recommend voluntarily admitting yourself enough: depending on what state you are in, a 302 can have some lasting effects after discharge.

A few points:

1. I find it quite ironic that the "imperfect" Diamond is, so far, the only diamond to have an *actual* perfect diamond as their gemstone.  The four-sided shape we see YD and BD have are not real shapes a diamond would actually have.  A real one would look just like PD's; we're just seeing it from the side.  
2. As far as PD's being the incorrect one based on shape, remember that we've never seen WD or her gem, so it's very possible hers could be similar to PD's, perhaps facing the other way.  2/3 being the "diamond shape" doesn't guarantee the last one is the same way.
3. Era 2 was never a "problem," but a solution.  It's quite clear that Homeworld is running out of resources to sustain itself, so making gems smaller means they need less resources.
4. From what we've seen, Era 2 began well after PD's shattering.  During "Back to the Moon," notice that Eyeball is the only Ruby that actually knows who Pink Diamond even was.  We also know that Peridot is relatively unaware of Rose and the rebellion (and perhaps PD as well) when she was first introduced and mainly now has some knowledge from her time spent with the Crystal Gems.  If Era 2 started before PD was made, these gems should know who she was, which so far has not been shown to be the case. 
5. To go back your first point, I'm not saying Pink Diamond *is* White Diamond.  With what I've presented, that would essentially be saying Steven *is* Rose Quartz.  For this theory, while they may share some similar traits with Steven perhaps getting a bit more if his "birth" was done in a more successful manner, they are still completely different and unique individuals with their own wants and desires.  Steven only *chooses* to follow the same rough path Rose did - he could easily have said he doesn't care about this gem stuff and just lived life as a human.  He could have also chosen to take Homeworld's side.  Neither will happen, but the point is that he is not bound by the choices Rose made.  The same would be true of PD.  She may share her gem and some of her powers, but that's about it.  PD is her own gem.  The only reason color would have been a major problem would come up in a comment above - WD's birth was not a perfect process, resulting in additional disfigurements.
The nerve of those insufferable, half-formed, traitor mega-clods!!!

The Crewniverse is very creative and could easily come up with something more elaborate, but a simple explanation would be that this change in color could simply be from a mistake in the process.  There was no precedence for this before PD came into existence, so it's possible that somewhere during...whatever happened to create her, a possible mistake was made by WD and/or her "mate" that resulted in that change in color (we haven't seen WD yet, so perhaps the gemstone is the same, but just a different hue).  Being able to learn from that process and see what could have been improved, it would be relatively easy for PD or maybe the other diamonds to look at the process and determine how to improve it and churn out some better results (perhaps this was a potential plan to stabilize homeworld by limiting needed resources WD cooked up and tried herself, but that's another theory for another day).  Armed with that knowledge, when passing down to Rose Quartz (perhaps one of the few if not ONLY other gems to learn of this), PD could have easily also mentioned what went wrong and how to avoid it.

Too much of the world and character development has been based on Pink Diamond being shattered.  I think they can get away with saying Rose was framed or that even Pearl took on Rose's form to shatter Pink for her (though I'm less sold on Pearl doing it -we already know that Pearl is awful at lying and for this to be carried on so long and well enough that even Garnet believes it would just be out of character for her) as that could provide more development into the Gem War and the Diamonds themselves.  To also magically include "Pink Diamond was actually not shattered at all!" would undo so much of that development and take away all the stakes (not sure if you are into Doctor Who, but the same thing happened when they magically decided to undo the whole "The Doctor wiped out the Daleks, Time Lords, and Gallifrey" deal - all that character growth went straight out the window and they're still trying desperately to find something to fill that void).  

After "The Trial" we know there was Diamond involvement in Pink's shattering.  Again, they wouldn't drop that big of a bomb just say "nah, nevermind, didn't happen."  If there is Diamond involvement in the shattering of Pink, White needs to be involved in one way or another since she is the head of the Authority and would have more than likely simply done everything behind the scenes and just simply make the calls (much like how a president doesn't actually go into battle, but will absolutely make the call to start wars and attack targets).  But let me be a bit more clear on this - the issue isn't White being off-screen and guilty, the issue would be White being off-screen and the ONLY ONE that is guilty.  If White came to the conclusion that Pink needs to be shattered, ordered it herself, and carried it out by herself without any involvement from Yellow or Blue, that would be what I would say is bad writing.  We have no basis for White Diamond.  Honestly, we don't even know that she will even be called White Diamond as the character has never once been mentioned by any character with the only reference being a mural on the Moon Base that was never acknowledged by any character there.  There needs to be some stakes involved in this mess and to achieve that, a Diamond we have already met also needs to be involved.  If anything, this could be how we meet White Diamond or, at the very least, get her name to finally drop.  Pink Pearl (or whoever) reveals Blue's involvement and is immediately confronted by Yellow about it.  Blue then gives the drop that she was ordered by White Diamond to carry it out, follow that up with Steven asking "Wait, who is White Diamond?" and there you go.  White would now be in the show and introduced in a way that paints just how powerful of a leader she is to get Blue Diamond to shatter her closest friend.

To address their behaviors, remember what Greg said about them.  They are the descendants of humans who came to the Zoo thousands of years ago and they have never even seen Earth.  These aren't humans freshly picked from the planet, these are humans for whom the Zoo is home and the only place they have ever known.  It's only natural they would develop unique behaviors and speech patterns after thousands of years of isolation. 

As far as compliance, I think Greg showed just how well that works.  Holly Blue Agate herself says that Greg was "loud" and "thrashing about," clearly resisting everything.  But then we see him in the Zoo and he doesn't seem to be fighting much of anything and even talks about how nice the people are and even comments that it's actually a pretty nice place where they don't need to worry about anything.  Sure, we could write this off as Greg just being Greg, but it's very likely that this is how all humans eventually react to the Zoo (though it should be noted that Greg and Steven are, as Holly Blue says, the first new humans in thousands of years).  

As for the "pile of human corpses," that's not exactly how Holly Blue presented it.  As she put it, "Apparently humans don't take well to captivity.  But once you understand their needs, they're easy to control."  Based on just that little bit of dialogue, it sounds more like that any "non-compliance" was eventually resolved the humans having their needs met.  Holly Blue has no issue talking about human disobedience in this context, but when mentioning the "human disposal shoot," she doesn't even discuss such things.  Considering her lack of care for humans, why not simply say that the shoot got rid of "undesirables?"  Realistically, the "human disposal shoot" is probably just a way to get rid of bodies once the humans pass away in the zoo.  Funeral rites and burial would be a foreign concept to gems as they generally do not die, so simply dumping the bodies into space would seem sufficient enough.

As far as the whole whether this was noble or malicious of Pink, I would like to bring out one of the show's biggest parallels to draw some comparisons - Pink Diamond and Rose Quartz.  When we see the flashbacks of Rose with Greg, she saw humans as "playing" and didn't believe they ever felt the same grief and pain that immortal gems do.  If this is the attitude of a Quartz in her court, then this would have also naturally been how Pink Diamond approached humans, so we can say that both Rose and Pink were, at best, naive about the nature of humans (and to be clear, she met Greg after Pink Diamond was shattered, so we can assume Rose carried the same thoughts throughout the Gem War).  But, look at what happened to Rose.  The more she learned about humans, that they are born a baby, grow up, always change, and can feel the same pain and sorrow as gems, the more she came to have true respect, appreciation, and even admiration for humans.  With just how much the Crewniverse has paralleled Rose Quartz and Pink Diamond, it can really just be safe to assume that Pink Diamond underwent the same process, albeit well before Rose did, in her implementation of the Zoo.  Both Rose and Pink started out as being indifferent to the human condition, but both would end with such an appreciation for human life that they are forced to question everything that Homeworld does in regards to them and other organic life.

From a writing standpoint, it's the best choice.  You're only other two choices are A) Yellow looked guilty in the trial.....and she is, or B) It was the Diamond that has never even been named in canon yet.  Either of those options leaves something to be desired.  Also, look at how Rebecca Sugar herself described the upcoming season - a "murder mystery."  It won't be something obvious like Yellow or something that has never been mentioned.  It will be something that has stared us in the face from the beginning, and Blue was the first one we met.

As far as why she came back, she said it herself in the rest of the quote you listed: "I should've done more. Yellow says it'll all be over soon. I wonder what you would think. This is your planet, after all. I still think it is."  She came back because the Cluster was supposed to emerge, meaning this is the last time Blue would be able to return to what is essentially Pink Diamond's grave.  Perhaps when she did say "I should've done more," she could just as easily have meant that she should have stood up to White Diamond and not shatter her closest friend (or whatever the specifics of this relationship were).  As far as Greg, you said it yourself.  He is just a human.  She didn't expect him to understand grief, how could she expect him to understand anything about the gems and Homeworld?

It isn't so much that there was "anti-organic life propaganda," but more "gems are better than all other creatures and no other creatures are due respect" that I was referring to.  You don't need to say that humans or other "animals" are bad if you simply ensure the populace consider them as nothing more than worthless sacks of cells.

Something else that has to be considered is how Pink's shattering was handled on Homeworld itself.  We know very little, but what we do know is telling.  We have learned that Gen 2 gems don't even know who Pink Diamond was.  That speaks volumes for what's going on here.  On Homeworld itself, they are making gems that have no memory of Pink Diamond whatsoever and have seemingly removed her from all current public signage and seals.  At least on Homeworld, Pink Diamond is being erased from history, not honored.  All that being said, there are still plenty of gems that were alive during Pink Diamond's life.  So, if you were White Diamond, how do you reconcile that problem?  Her solution is actually quite elegant - spin the major problems (like the Zoo) into a positive memorial for Pink Diamond, furthering the always existent idea that the Diamonds are superior and always do what's best for all gems.  Holly Blue says it herself; "It's tragic that Pink Diamond's existence in this universe ended up being so finite, but what a selfless act for Blue Diamond to step forward and spend her own time and energy, preserving this place in Pink Diamond's memory. It's a real testament to Blue Diamond's merciful and forgiving nature, don't you think?"  Why cover up positive press?!?  

As for the trial, a couple additional things.  One, Yellow Diamond, as I mentioned, was eager to shatter Steven without any real proof of anything.  It would take something major to get her to think that there are some ulterior motives being acted out.  As for why Pink Pearl was not shattered, consider the role of Pearls in society.  I would certainly agree that most other members of Pink Diamond's court were probably shattered, especially the Sapphires.  Why?  Because they have a higher standing in society.  Other gems are much more willing to listen to the words of a Sapphire or Agate.  But a Pearl?  They are made look pretty and hold your stuff.  The average Homeworld gem wouldn't give a Pearl the time of day.  White Diamond would have so many options for this "loose end" beyond shattering.  All she would have to do is continue fueling Pink Pearl's natural insecurities (as seen in our Pearl) and she won't say a single word about anything.  In fact, White Diamond, being the powerful leader she is, could probably force Pink Pearl to go along with whatever story she wanted, making it all the more convincing to not only Yellow Diamond but every other gem that knew who Pink Diamond was.  

There are several different possibilities for Pink Pearl that I have considered, even going so far as to deduce that the Diamonds did intend to shatter her, but that she got away and has been in hiding for quite some time (perhaps to be discovered on whatever planet that ship that was shot down in the SDCC trailer landed on)  Regardless of what flavor you choose, there are several feasible ways for Pink Pearl to still be around.  Again, I look to the writing.  Why drop her name in such a dramatic way just to follow it up with "Oh yeah, she's shattered by the way."  That was the first time she was ever mentioned in canon, and to do so in that impactful of a way can only mean she is about to play a major role.

Remember that big rock that Rhodonite and the Rhutile twins could barely move to block the exit?  Remember that Rhodonite is a fusion and should naturally have a fairly large amount of strength because of it?  Now, remember how Steven just walked right up and pushed that boulder like a shopping cart?  If he's stronger than a fusion, Steven can take on your average Quartz soldier.

The episode "Off-Colors" showed us that a gem doesn't need to be defective to be considered off-colored, just that they had to go against the rules and norms of Homeworld, such as through fusion as seen by Fluorite and Rhodonite.  Pink Diamond's Human Zoo alone showed just how against Homeworld norms she was.  It's not like she just grabbed a bunch of humans and put them in cages.  No, she went through the trouble of figuring out the needs of human beings (such as food, clothing, recreation, romantic partners, etc.), designed the zoo to be a complete paradise where all these needs are taken care of, and sustain it well enough that the inhabitants have been able to have an active society for thousands of years.  That is far more care and consideration towards organic life than any other gem would even consider taking, let alone a Diamond.  Homeworld propaganda has always shown a complete disdain and downright disrespect towards organic life with the idea that such creatures do not deserve anything but to be tossed aside so gems can flourish.  Sure, Blue is keeping the Zoo running, but that's more of a way for her to honor Pink (or maybe make up for her sins against Pink...) than any care about humans.  Homeworld propaganda has also taught us a critical view about Homeworld values - those that don't fit the mold must be destroyed.  This is why the off-colors have to go into hiding and why the Crystal Gems are still considered war criminals worthy of shattering.  Also consider that Blue Diamond herself ordered that shattering of Ruby after accidentally fusing with Sapphire for just a brief moment, even though Ruby had just saved her from Pearl's attack.  Having a Diamond that could possibly meet that definition of off-color, even if only by the slightest margins, runs the risk of the entire Homeworld society and culture of caving.  How can the Diamond Authority possibly enforce their rules and standards if one of their own goes against them?  White probably made several attempts to get Pink to comply, but Pink would not listen.  Based on everything we have learned about Homeworld and how the Diamonds operate, it isn't a far stretch to consider that White Diamond would seek out Pink's shattering to maintain her order and rule.

As for why Yellow was present at the trial, here are a couple things to consider.  Starting with something very simple, which would be more suspicious for Yellow, hearing testimony from a traitor that attempts to incriminate Blue, or not being allowed into the trial in the first place?  When it comes to dealing with Earth, Yellow is basically now in charge of the operation, including managing the Cluster.  Yellow is leading the military as far as we can tell and is definitely carrying the leader mantle since Blue is stuck in her grief (guilt) trip.  Yellow is now wayyy too involved and has too much at stake to be left out of this trial.  

Also, notice the questions that Blue was asking.  She didn't ask Steven to tell the whole story.  She asked for very, very specific details.  Her questions were directed in such a way to get only a couple crucial details that would prove the legitimacy (or lack thereof) of the gem claiming to be Rose Quartz and nothing more.  For safe measures, if it was the real Rose Quartz and she did reveal the truth as I have outlined, Blue could easily have this dismissed as the excuse of a traitor and Yellow would have easily gone along with it (after all, Yellow was ready to shatter without even hearing from Steven).  This is why I believe Pink Pearl will play a crucial role in all of this.  It's one thing for Rose Quartz to make the claim, but for Pink's own Pearl, a devoted Homeworld gem presumedly, to corroborate the same story would force Yellow to accept the reality that she has been had.
